title.zh: 卷10 列傳第2 邵惠公顥 杞簡公連 莒莊公洛生 虞國公仲
title.en: Volume 10 Biographies 2: Duke Hao of Shaohui; Duke Lian of Qijian; Duke Luosheng of Juzhuang; Duke Zhong of Yuguo
title.raw: 卷10 列傳第2 邵惠公顥 杞簡公連 莒莊公洛生 虞國公仲 Volume 10 Biographies 2: Duke Hao of Shaohui; Duke Lian of Qijian; Duke Luosheng of Juzhuang; Duke Zhong of Yuguo

sentences.zh: 邵惠公顥 子什肥 導

translations.literal: Duke Hui of Shao Hao; sons Shifen, Dao
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hui of Shao Yuwen Hao; sons Shifen and Yuwen Dao

translations.literal: (Hu)
translations.idiomatic: (Hu)

sentences.zh: 什肥子胄 導子廣 亮 翼 椿 衆 杞簡公連 莒莊公洛生 子菩提 虞國公仲 子興

translations.literal: Shifen's son Zhou; Dao's sons Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, Zhong; Duke Jian of Qi Lian; Duke Zhuang of Ju Luosheng; son Puti; Duke Zhong of Yuguo Zhong; son Xing
translations.idiomatic: Shifen's son Yuwen Zhou; Yuwen Dao's sons Guang, Liang, Yi, Chun, and Zhong; Duke Jian of Qi Yuwen Lian; Duke Zhuang of Ju Yuwen Luosheng; son Puti; Duke Zhong of Yuguo Yuwen Zhong; son Xing

sentences.zh: 邵惠公顥，太祖之長兄也。

translations.literal: Duke Hui of Shao Hao was the Grand Progenitor's eldest elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hui of Shao Yuwen Hao was the elder brother of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 德皇帝娶樂浪王氏，是為德皇后。

translations.literal: Emperor De married Lady Wang of Lelang; she became Empress De.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor De married Lady Wang of Lelang; she became Empress De.

sentences.zh: 生顥，次杞簡公連，次莒莊公洛生，次太祖。

translations.literal: She bore Hao, then Duke Jian of Qi Lian, then Duke Zhuang of Ju Luosheng, then the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Yuwen Hao, then Duke Jian of Qi Yuwen Lian, then Duke Zhuang of Ju Yuwen Luosheng, and finally Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 顥性至孝，德皇后崩，哀毀過禮，鄉黨咸敬異焉。

translations.literal: Hao was supremely filial; when Empress De died, his grief exceeded ritual propriety, and neighbors all admired him in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hao was supremely filial; when Empress De died, his mourning went beyond ritual bounds, and all in the neighborhood looked on him with respect and wonder.

sentences.zh: 德皇帝與衛可孤戰於武川南河，臨陣墜馬，顥與數騎奔救，擊殺數十人，賊衆披靡，德皇帝乃得上馬引去。

translations.literal: Emperor De fought Wei Kegu at the Southern River of Wuchuan; he fell from his horse in battle. Hao with several horsemen rushed to the rescue, killed dozens of men, the enemy host scattered, and Emperor De was able to mount and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor De fought Wei Kegu at the Southern River of Wuchuan and fell from his horse in the field, Yuwen Hao galloped to his aid with a few riders, cut down dozens of the enemy, put their force to flight, and enabled Emperor De to remount and escape.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊追騎大至，顥遂戰歿。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy pursuit cavalry arrived in force, and Hao then died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the enemy pursuit cavalry came up in strength, and Yuwen Hao fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈太師、柱國大將軍、大冢宰、大都督、恆朔等十州諸軍事、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, pillar-of-state grand general, grand chancellor, chief commander, commander of all military affairs in ten provinces including Heng and Shuo, and governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), Yuwen Hao was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, pillar-of-state grand general, grand chancellor, chief commander, commander of all military affairs in ten provinces including Heng and Shuo, and governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 封邵國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao state, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao, with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 諡曰惠。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Hui (Kind).

sentences.zh: 顥三子什肥、導、護。

translations.literal: Hao had three sons: Shifen, Dao, and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hao had three sons: Shifen, Yuwen Dao, and Yuwen Hu.

sentences.zh: 護別有傳。

translations.literal: Hu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 什肥年十五而惠公歿，自傷早孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shifen was fifteen when Duke Hui died; grieving his early orphanhood, he served his mother with filial piety that became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen was fifteen when Duke Hui died; grieving his early loss, he served his mother with a filial devotion that became renowned.

sentences.zh: 永安中，太祖入關，什肥不能離母，遂留晉陽。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era (528–530), the Grand Progenitor entered Guan; Shifen could not leave his mother and therefore remained at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era (528–530), when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai entered Guan, Shifen could not leave his mother and remained at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及太祖定秦、隴，什肥為齊神武所害。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor had pacified Qin and Long, Shifen was killed by Duke of Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: After Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had pacified Qin and Long, Shifen was killed by Gao Huan, Duke of Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小冢宰、大都督、冀定等州諸軍事、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was posthumously granted grand general, junior grand chancellor, chief commander, commander of all military affairs in Ji and Ding provinces, and governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), Shifen was posthumously granted grand general, junior grand chancellor, chief commander, commander of all military affairs in Ji and Ding provinces, and governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 襲爵邵國公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Shao state.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 諡曰景。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jing (Resplendent).

sentences.zh: 子冑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuwen Zhou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 冑少而孤貧，頗有乾略。

translations.literal: Zhou was orphaned young and poor, yet had considerable initiative and strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhou was orphaned young and poor, yet showed considerable drive and strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 景公之見害也，以年幼下蠶室。

translations.literal: When Duke Jing was killed, because of his young age he was sent to the castration quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Jing was killed, Yuwen Zhou, because of his youth, was sent to the castration quarters.

sentences.zh: 保定初，詔以晉公護子會紹景公封。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, an edict ordered that Duke of Jin Hu's son Hui should succeed to Duke Jing's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), an edict ordered that Yuwen Hui, son of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, should succeed to Duke Jing's enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 天和中，與齊通好，冑始歸關中。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era (566–572), when peace with Qi was established, Zhou first returned to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era (566–572), when peace was made with Northern Qi, Yuwen Zhou first returned to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 授大將軍、開府儀同三司，襲爵邵公。

translations.literal: He was granted grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and inherited the title Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, and inherited the title Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 尋除宗師中大夫，進位大將軍，出為原州刺史，轉滎州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee, advanced to grand general, sent out as governor of Yuan Province, and transferred to governor of Xing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed master-of-clans middle grandee, advanced to grand general, sent out as governor of Yuan Province, and transferred to governor of Xing Province.

sentences.zh: 大象末，隋文帝輔政，冑舉州兵應尉遲迥，與清河公楊素戰，敗，遂走，追獲於石濟，遂斬之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era (579–581), when Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, Zhou raised the provincial troops to support Yuchi Jiong; he fought Prince of Qinghe Yang Su, was defeated, fled, was captured at Shiji, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era (579–581), when Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, served as regent, Yuwen Zhou raised provincial troops to support Yuchi Jiong; he fought Yang Su, Duke of Qinghe, was defeated, fled, was captured at Shiji, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 國除。

translations.literal: The state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The ducal fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: （冑子）

translations.literal: (Zhou's son)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhou's son)

sentences.zh: 〔會字〕乾仁，幼好學，聰惠。

translations.literal: [Hui, style name] Ganren; as a child he loved learning and was clever and bright.
translations.idiomatic: [Yuwen Hui, style name Ganren] loved learning from childhood and was clever and bright.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，以護平江陵之功，賜爵江陵縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wei Emperor Gong (555), for Hu's merit in pacifying Jiangling, he was granted the title Marquis of Jiangling county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Western Wei Emperor Gong (555), for Yuwen Hu's merit in pacifying Jiangling, he was granted the title Marquis of Jiangling county.

sentences.zh: 保定初，紹景公後，拜驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he succeeded after Duke Jing and was appointed flying-cavalry grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), he succeeded after Duke Jing and was appointed flying-cavalry grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol.

sentences.zh: 二年，除蒲州潼關六防諸軍事、蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed commander of the six garrisons of Tong Pass at Pu Province and governor of Pu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (562), he was appointed commander of the six garrisons of Tong Pass at Pu Province and governor of Pu Province.

sentences.zh: 冑至自齊，改封譚國公。

translations.literal: When Zhou returned from Qi, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Tan state.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Zhou returned from Northern Qi, Yuwen Hui's enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 尋進位柱國。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 建德初，與護同伏誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande (572), he was executed together with Hu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jiande (572), he was executed together with Yuwen Hu.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，追贈，復封舊爵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, he was posthumously honored and his former enfeoffment was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year (574), he was posthumously honored and his former enfeoffment was restored.

sentences.zh: 導字菩薩。

translations.literal: Dao, style name Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Dao, style name Pusa.

sentences.zh: 少雄豪，有仁惠，太祖愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and heroic, possessed benevolence and kindness, and the Grand Progenitor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and heroic, possessed benevolence and kindness, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai loved him.

sentences.zh: 初與諸父在葛榮軍中，榮敗，遷晉陽。

translations.literal: At first he was with his uncles in Ge Rong's army; when Rong was defeated, they were relocated to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was with his uncles in Ge Rong's army; when Ge Rong was defeated, they were relocated to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及太祖隨賀拔岳入關，導從而西，常從征伐。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor followed Helba Yue into Guan, Dao followed west and constantly joined the campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai followed Helba Yue into Guan, Yuwen Dao followed west and constantly joined the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 太祖討侯莫陳悅，以導為都督，鎮原州。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Houmochen Yue and made Dao commander, garrisoning Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai campaigned against Houmochen Yue, he made Yuwen Dao commander and garrisoned Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 及悅敗，北走出故塞，導率騎追之，至牽屯山及悅，斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: When Yue was defeated and fled north through the old frontier pass, Dao led cavalry in pursuit, reached Qiantun Mountain, caught Yue, beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue was defeated and fled north through the old frontier pass, Yuwen Dao led cavalry in pursuit, caught him at Qiantun Mountain, beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以功封饒陽縣侯，邑五百戶，拜冠軍將軍，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Raoyang county, fief of five hundred households, appointed Champion General, and given the additional post of Regular Attendant through direct connection.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Raoyang county with a fief of five hundred households, appointed Champion General, and given the additional post of Regular Attendant through direct connection.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝卽位，以定策功，進爵為公，增邑五百戶，拜使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Wei Emperor Wen acceded, for merit in settling the succession he was advanced to duke, his fief was increased by five hundred households, and he was appointed bearer of staff of authority, Regular Attendant Imperial Secretary, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei Emperor Wen acceded, for merit in settling the succession he was advanced to duke, his fief was increased by five hundred households, and he was appointed bearer of staff of authority, Regular Attendant Imperial Secretary, chariots-and-cavalry grand general, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 三年，太祖東征，導入宿衛，拜領軍將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Grand Progenitor marched east; Dao entered palace guard service and was appointed director of the guard and chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (535), when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched east, Yuwen Dao entered palace guard service and was appointed director of the guard and chief commander.

sentences.zh: 齊神武渡河侵馮翊，太祖自弘農引軍入關，導督左右禁旅會於沙苑，與齊神武戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Shenwu crossed the river and invaded Fengyi; the Grand Progenitor led his army into Guan from Hongnong. Dao directed the left and right imperial guard, joined at Shaye, fought Duke of Qi Shenwu, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan, Duke of Qi Shenwu, crossed the river and invaded Fengyi, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai led his army into Guan from Hongnong. Yuwen Dao directed the left and right imperial guard, joined at Shaye, fought Gao Huan, and inflicted a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 進位儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced to commissioner equal to Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to commissioner equal to Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏文帝東征，留導為華州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year, when Wei Emperor Wen marched east, Dao was left as governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Western Wei Emperor Wen marched east, Yuwen Dao was left as governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 及趙青雀、于伏德、慕容思慶等作亂，導自華州率所部兵擊之，擒伏德，斬思慶。

translations.literal: When Zhao Qingque, Yu Fude, Murong Siqing, and others rebelled, Dao from Hua Province led his troops against them, captured Fude, and beheaded Siqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Qingque, Yu Fude, Murong Siqing, and others rebelled, Yuwen Dao from Hua Province led his troops against them, captured Yu Fude, and beheaded Murong Siqing.

sentences.zh: 進屯渭橋，會太祖軍。

translations.literal: He advanced to camp at Wei Bridge and joined the Grand Progenitor's army.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to camp at Wei Bridge and joined Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's army.

sentences.zh: 事平，進爵章武郡公，增邑並前二千戶。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Zhangwu commandery, and his fief together with the former totaled two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Zhangwu commandery, and his fief together with the former totaled two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中、開府、驃騎大將軍、太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given palace attendant, commissioner, flying-cavalry grand general, and junior tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally given palace attendant, commissioner, flying-cavalry grand general, and junior tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 高仲密以北豫降，太祖率諸將輔魏皇太子東征，復以導為大都督、華東雍二州諸軍事，行華州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered Beiyu, the Grand Progenitor led the generals in supporting the Wei crown prince on an eastern campaign; Dao was again made chief commander of military affairs in Hua, East Yong, and the two Yong provinces, and acting governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered Beiyu, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai led the generals in supporting the Western Wei crown prince on an eastern campaign; Yuwen Dao was again made chief commander of military affairs in Hua, East Yong, and the two Yong provinces, and acting governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 導治兵訓卒，得守捍之方。

translations.literal: Dao trained troops and drilled soldiers and mastered methods of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Dao trained troops and drilled soldiers and mastered methods of defense.

sentences.zh: 及大軍不利，東魏軍追至稠桑，知關中有備，乃退。

translations.literal: When the main army suffered a setback, the Eastern Wei army pursued as far as Chousang; learning that Guanzhong was prepared, they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army suffered a setback, the Eastern Wei army pursued as far as Chousang; learning that Guanzhong was prepared, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會侯景舉河南來附，遣使請援，朝議將應之，乃徵為隴右大都督、秦南等十五州諸軍事、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered Henan and came over, sending envoys to request aid, the court debated responding; Dao was then summoned as chief commander of Longyou, commander of all military affairs in fifteen provinces including Qinnan, and governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing surrendered Henan and came over, sending envoys to request aid, the court debated responding; Yuwen Dao was then summoned as chief commander of Longyou, commander of all military affairs in fifteen provinces including Qinnan, and governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 及齊氏稱帝，太祖發關中兵討之，魏文帝遣齊王廓鎮隴右，徵導還朝。

translations.literal: When the Qi house declared itself emperor, the Grand Progenitor dispatched Guanzhong troops to campaign against it; Wei Emperor Wen sent Prince of Qi Kuo to garrison Longyou and summoned Dao back to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi declared itself emperor, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai dispatched Guanzhong troops to campaign against it; Western Wei Emperor Wen sent Prince of Qi Kuo to garrison Longyou and summoned Yuwen Dao back to court.

sentences.zh: 拜大將軍、大都督、三雍二華等二十三州諸軍事，屯咸陽。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand general, chief commander of all military affairs in twenty-three provinces including the Three Yong and Two Hua, and garrisoned Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand general, chief commander of all military affairs in twenty-three provinces including the Three Yong and Two Hua, and garrisoned Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 大軍還，乃旋舊鎮。

translations.literal: When the main army returned, he then returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army returned, he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 初，廣母李氏以廣患彌年，憂而成疾，因此致沒。

translations.literal: At first, Guang's mother Lady Li, because Guang's illness had lasted years, worried herself into sickness and thereby died.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Yuwen Guang's mother Lady Li, because Guang's illness had lasted years, worried herself into sickness and thereby died.

sentences.zh: 廣旣居喪，更加綿篤，乃以毀薨。

translations.literal: Guang having entered mourning, his illness grew still worse, and he died from grief-induced destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Guang having entered mourning, his illness grew still worse, and he died from grief-induced destruction.

sentences.zh: 世稱母為廣病，廣為母亡，慈孝之道，極於一門。

translations.literal: The age said the mother died of Guang's illness and Guang died for his mother—filial piety and kindness reached their utmost in one clan.
translations.idiomatic: The age said the mother died of Guang's illness and Guang died for his mother—filial piety and kindness reached their utmost in one clan.

sentences.zh: 高祖素服親臨，百僚畢集。

translations.literal: High Ancestor in plain white mourning garb personally attended; the hundred officials all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong in plain white mourning garb personally attended; the hundred officials all assembled.

sentences.zh: 其故吏儀同李充信等上表曰：

translations.literal: His former subordinate commissioner-equal Li Chongxin and others submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: His former subordinate commissioner-equal Li Chongxin and others submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣等接事，每承餘論。

translations.literal: We who served under him often received his leftover teachings.
translations.idiomatic: We who served under him often received his parting counsels.

sentences.zh: 仰之平昔，約己立身，位極上公，賦兼千乘，所獲祿秩，周贍無餘，器用服玩，取給而已。

translations.literal: Looking up to his past conduct, he restrained himself in self-cultivation; his rank reached supreme duke, his revenues matched a thousand chariots; the salary and stipends he received fully provided for his dependents without remainder; utensils and luxury goods he took only as sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to his past conduct, he restrained himself in self-cultivation; his rank reached supreme duke, his revenues matched a thousand chariots; the salary and stipends he received fully provided for his dependents without remainder; utensils and luxury goods he took only as sufficed.

sentences.zh: 每言及終始，尤存簡素。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of life and death, he especially maintained simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of life and death, he especially maintained simplicity.

sentences.zh: 非秦政而褒吳禮，譏石椁而美厚薪。

translations.literal: He did not praise Wu's burial rites like Qin Zheng, ridicule stone coffins while praising thick firewood.
translations.idiomatic: He did not praise Wu's burial rites like the First Emperor of Qin, ridicule stone coffins while praising thick firewood.

sentences.zh: 今卜兆有期，先遠方及，誠恐一從朝露，此志莫伸。

translations.literal: Now the burial site has been divined and a date set, and the distant ancestors approach; we truly fear that once the morning dew falls, this wish cannot be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Now the burial site has been divined and a date set, and the distant ancestors approach; we truly fear that once death comes like morning dew, this wish cannot be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下弘不世之慈，垂霈然之澤，留情旣往，降愍幽魂，爰勑有司，申其宿志，窀穸之禮，庶存儉約。

translations.literal: We humbly hope Your Majesty will extend unprecedented kindness, bestow pouring grace, remember the departed, show pity to the hidden soul, command the offices to fulfill his lifelong wish, and keep the burial rites frugal.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly hope Your Majesty will extend unprecedented kindness, bestow pouring grace, remember the departed, show pity to the hidden soul, command the offices to fulfill his lifelong wish, and keep the burial rites frugal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「省充信等表，但增哀悼。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Having read Chongxin and the others' memorial, mourning is only increased.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Having read Chongxin and the others' memorial, mourning is only increased.

sentences.zh: 豳國公廣藩屏令望，宗室表儀，言著身文，行成士則。

translations.literal: Duke of Bin state Guang, screen of the realm and excellent reputation, model of the imperial clan, words manifest in conduct, conduct forms a gentleman's standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Guang, Duke of Bin, screen of the realm and excellent reputation, model of the imperial clan, words manifest in conduct, conduct forms a gentleman's standard.

sentences.zh: 方憑懿戚，用匡朝政，奄丁荼蓼，便致毀滅。

translations.literal: Just when one relied on excellent kin to assist court government, he suddenly met bitter hardship and was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Just when one relied on excellent kin to assist court government, he suddenly met bitter hardship and was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 啟手歸全，無忘雅操。

translations.literal: He opened his hands and returned whole, never forgetting elegant integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his hands and returned whole, never forgetting elegant integrity.

sentences.zh: 言念旣往，震于厥心。

translations.literal: Speaking of the past, the heart is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of the past, the heart is shaken.

sentences.zh: 昔河間才藻，追敘於中尉；

translations.literal: Formerly Hejian's literary talent was commemorated by the Commandant of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Hejian's literary talent was commemorated by the Commandant of Justice;

sentences.zh: 東海謙約，見稱於身後。

translations.literal: Donghai's modest restraint was praised after death.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai's modest restraint was praised after death.

sentences.zh: 可斟酌前典，率由舊章。

translations.literal: May former canons be consulted and old regulations followed.
translations.idiomatic: May former canons be consulted and old regulations followed.

sentences.zh: 使易簀之言，得申遺志；

translations.literal: Let the words of changing the mat fulfill his dying wish;
translations.idiomatic: Let the words of changing the mat fulfill his dying wish;

sentences.zh: 黜殯之請，無虧令終。

translations.literal: the request to dismiss lavish burial not mar his fine end.
translations.idiomatic: the request to dismiss lavish burial not mar his fine end.

sentences.zh: 」於是贈本官，加太保。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was granted his former office and additionally made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he was granted his former office and additionally made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 葬於隴西。

translations.literal: He was buried in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 所司一遵詔旨，竝存儉約。

translations.literal: The responsible offices all followed the edict and together kept frugal simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices all followed the edict and together kept frugal simplicity.

sentences.zh: 子洽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qia succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qia succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大定中，隋文輔政，以宗室被害，國除。

translations.literal: In the Dading era (581), when Sui Wen served as regent, because members of the imperial clan were killed, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era (581), when Yang Jian served as regent, because members of the imperial clan were killed, the ducal fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 亮字乾德。

translations.literal: Liang, style name Gandé.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Liang, style name Gandé.

sentences.zh: 武成初，封永昌郡公。

translations.literal: In the early Wucheng era (559), he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wucheng era (559), he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 後襲烈公爵，除開府儀同三司、梁州總管。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke Lie and was appointed commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and governor-general of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited the title Duke Lie and was appointed commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and governor-general of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 天和末，拜宗師中大夫，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianhe, he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee and advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianhe (572), he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee and advanced to grand general.

sentences.zh: 豳國公薨，以亮為秦州總管，廣之所部，悉以配焉。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Bin died, Liang was made governor-general of Qin Province, and all troops formerly under Guang were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Guang, Duke of Bin, died, Yuwen Liang was made governor-general of Qin Province, and all troops formerly under Guang were assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 亮在州甚無政績。

translations.literal: Liang in the province had very little administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Liang achieved very little in governing the province.

sentences.zh: 尋進位柱國。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 晉公護誅後，亮心不自安，唯縱酒而已。

translations.literal: After Duke of Jin Hu was executed, Liang's heart was uneasy, and he indulged only in wine.
translations.idiomatic: After Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was executed, Yuwen Liang's heart was uneasy, and he indulged only in wine.

sentences.zh: 高祖手勑讓之。

translations.literal: High Ancestor personally wrote a reprimanding edict.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong personally wrote a reprimanding edict.

sentences.zh: 建德中，高祖東伐，以亮為右第二軍總管。

translations.literal: During Jiande (572–578), when High Ancestor marched east, Liang was made commander of the second army on the right.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiande (572–578), when High Ancestor Yuwen Yong marched east, Yuwen Liang was made commander of the second army on the right.

sentences.zh: 幷州平，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: When Bing Province was pacified, he was advanced to superior pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing Province was pacified, he was advanced to superior pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 仍從平鄴，遷大司徒。

translations.literal: He still followed in pacifying Ye and was transferred to Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He still followed in pacifying Ye and was transferred to Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 宣帝卽位，出為安州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was sent out as governor-general of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun acceded, he was sent out as governor-general of An Province.

sentences.zh: 大象初，詔以亮為行軍總管，與元帥、鄖國公韋孝寬等伐陳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, an edict appointed Liang campaign commander-in-chief; together with the commander-in-chief Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, and others he attacked Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daxiang era (579), an edict made Yuwen Liang campaign commander-in-chief; with the supreme commander Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, and others he marched against Chen.

sentences.zh: 亮自安陸道攻拔黃城，輒破江側民村，掠其生口，以賜士卒。

translations.literal: Liang by the Anlu route captured Huangcheng, repeatedly raided villages on the river's south bank, took captives, and distributed them to the troops as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Liang took the Anlu route, captured Huangcheng, repeatedly plundered riverside villages, seized captives, and gave them to his soldiers as booty.

sentences.zh: 軍還至豫州，亮密謂長史杜士峻曰：「主上淫縱滋甚，社稷將危。

translations.literal: When the army returned to Yu Province, Liang secretly said to Chief Clerk Du Shijun: "The sovereign's debauchery grows ever worse; the altars of state are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Yu Province, Liang secretly told Chief Clerk Du Shijun: "The emperor's excess grows worse by the day and the realm is in danger.

sentences.zh: 吾旣忝宗枝，不忍坐見傾覆。

translations.literal: I am already of the imperial clan; I cannot bear to sit by and watch ruin.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the royal house, I cannot sit idle while everything collapses.

sentences.zh: 今若襲取鄖國公而幷其衆，推諸父為主，鼓行而前，誰敢不從。

translations.literal: If we now seize the Duke of Yun and merge his forces, install one of the paternal uncles as ruler, and advance with drums beating, who would dare not follow?"
translations.idiomatic: If we surprise the Duke of Yun, take his army, set up one of our uncles as ruler, and march forward to the drum, who would refuse to follow?"

sentences.zh: 」遂夜將數百騎襲孝寬營。

translations.literal: " Thereupon by night he led several hundred horsemen in a surprise attack on Xiaokuan's camp.
translations.idiomatic: " That night he led several hundred riders in a night assault on Xiaokuan's camp.

sentences.zh: 會亮國官茹寬知其謀，先以馳告，孝寬乃設備。

translations.literal: As it happened, Liang's household officer Ru Kuan learned of the plot and first sent a fast rider to report it; Xiaokuan thereupon made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's household officer Ru Kuan learned of the plot, sent word ahead by fast courier, and Xiaokuan made ready.

sentences.zh: 亮不克，遯走，孝寬追斬之。

translations.literal: Liang did not succeed, fled, and Xiaokuan pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang failed, fled, and Xiaokuan ran him down and executed him.

sentences.zh: 子明坐亮誅。

translations.literal: His son Ming was executed because of Liang's crime.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ming was put to death on account of Liang's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔以亮弟椿為烈公後。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Liang's younger brother Chun to continue the line of Duke Lie.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Liang's younger brother Chun heir to Duke Lie.

sentences.zh: 翼字乾宜。

translations.literal: Yi, style Qianyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Qianyi.

sentences.zh: 武成初，封西陽郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Wucheng era he received the title Duke of Xiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 早薨，諡曰昭。

translations.literal: He died young; his posthumous title was Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He died young and was posthumously titled Zhao.

sentences.zh: 無子，以杞國公亮子溫為嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, Wen, son of Liang, Duke of Qi, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, so Wen, son of Yuwen Liang, Duke of Qi, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 後坐亮反誅，國除。

translations.literal: Later, because of Liang's rebellion, Wen was executed and the fief abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wen was executed for Liang's revolt and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 衆字乾道。

translations.literal: Zhong, style Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, styled Qiandao.

sentences.zh: 保定初，封天水郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Baoding era he was enfeoffed Duke of Tianshui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少而不惠，語默不常，人莫能測。

translations.literal: From youth he was dull-witted; in speech and silence he was unpredictable, and no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was slow-witted; his words and silences were erratic, and no one could read him.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，初欲封為介公，後復誅之，幷二子仲和、孰倫。

translations.literal: When Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian took the throne, at first he intended to enfeoff Zhong as Duke of Jie, but later executed him together with his two sons Zhonghe and Shulun.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian ascended, he first meant to make Zhong Duke of Jie, but later had him killed along with his sons Zhonghe and Shulun.

sentences.zh: 杞簡公連，幼而謹厚，臨敵果毅。

translations.literal: Duke Lian of Qi, Lian, from youth was careful and honest, and in battle resolute and daring.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Lian of Qi, Yuwen Lian, was careful and honest from childhood and resolute in battle.

sentences.zh: 隨德皇帝逼定州，軍於唐河，遂俱歿。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor De in pressing Ding Province, encamped at the Tang River, and there both perished.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor De in the advance on Ding Province, camped on the Tang River, and there both died.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈使持節、太傅、柱國大將軍、大司徒、大都督、定冀等十州諸軍事、定州刺史；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ding, Ji, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Ding Province;
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Ding, Ji, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Ding Province;

sentences.zh: 封杞國公，邑五千戶；

translations.literal: enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, with a fief of five thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed Duke of Qi, with a fief of five thousand households;

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡。

translations.literal: posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: and given the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 子

translations.literal: Son
translations.idiomatic: His son

translations.literal: (Guang)
translations.idiomatic: (Guang)

sentences.zh: 〔元〕寶為齊神武所害。

translations.literal: [Yuan] Bao was killed by Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: [Yuan] Bao was killed by Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小司徒、〔大〕都督、幽燕等六州諸軍事、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted grand general, junior minister of education, [grand] governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in You, Yan, and six other provinces, and inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made grand general, junior minister of education, [grand] governor-general, commander-in-chief over You, Yan, and six other provinces, and inspector of You Province.

sentences.zh: 襲爵杞國公，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Qi; posthumous title Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the dukedom of Qi and received the posthumous title Lie.

sentences.zh: 以章武公導子亮嗣。

translations.literal: Liang, son of Duke of Zhangwu Dao, succeeded to the line.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Liang, son of Duke of Zhangwu Dao, became heir.

sentences.zh: 莒莊公洛生，少任俠，尚武藝，及壯，有大度，好施愛士。

translations.literal: Duke Luosheng of Ju, from youth was chivalrous and martial; when grown he had great breadth of mind and loved to be generous and cherish men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Luosheng of Ju, Yuwen Luosheng, was a young bravo who loved arms; grown, he was magnanimous, generous, and fond of nurturing talent.

sentences.zh: 北州賢俊，皆與之遊，而才能多出其下。

translations.literal: Worthy and outstanding men of the northern provinces all associated with him, yet in talent most fell below him.
translations.idiomatic: The best men of the northern provinces sought his company, yet few matched his ability.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮破鮮于修禮，乃以洛生為漁陽王，仍領德皇帝餘衆。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong defeated Xianyu Xiuli, he thereupon made Luosheng Prince of Yuyang and still commanded the remaining forces of Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong defeated Xianyu Xiuli, he made Luosheng Prince of Yuyang and left him in command of Emperor De's remaining troops.

sentences.zh: 時人皆呼為洛生王。

translations.literal: People of the time all called him Prince Luosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called him the Luosheng Prince.

sentences.zh: 洛生善將士，帳下多驍勇。

translations.literal: Luosheng was skilled in commanding troops; under his banner were many fierce warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Luosheng knew how to lead soldiers, and many bold fighters served under his banner.

sentences.zh: 至於攻戰，莫有當其鋒者，是以克獲常冠諸軍。

translations.literal: In attack and battle none could withstand his spearhead; therefore his captures and gains usually led all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In battle none could stand before his vanguard, and his victories usually topped those of every other army.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮定山東，收諸豪傑，遷於晉陽，洛生時在虜中。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong pacified Shandong he gathered the regional champions and relocated them to Jinyang; Luosheng was then among the captives.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong settled Shandong he gathered local strongmen and moved them to Jinyang; Luosheng was among the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 榮雅聞其名，心憚之。

translations.literal: Rong had long heard his name and inwardly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong had long known his reputation and feared him in his heart.

sentences.zh: 尋為榮所害。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was killed by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Rong had him killed.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈使持節、太保、柱國大將軍、大冢宰、大宗伯、大都督、幷肆等十州諸軍事、幷州刺史；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted commissioner bearing credentials, grand guardian, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of tombs, grand clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Bing, Si, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Bing Province;
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made commissioner bearing credentials, grand guardian, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of tombs, grand clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Bing, Si, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Bing Province;

sentences.zh: 封莒國公，邑五千戶；

translations.literal: enfeoffed as Duke of Ju, with a fief of five thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed Duke of Ju, with a fief of five thousand households;

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊。

translations.literal: posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: and given the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子菩提，為齊神武所害。

translations.literal: His son Puti was killed by Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Puti was killed by Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈大將軍、小宗伯、大都督、肆恆等六州諸軍事、肆州刺史，襲爵莒國公，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted grand general, junior clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Si, Heng, and six other provinces, and inspector of Si Province; he inherited the title Duke of Ju; posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made grand general, junior clan elder, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Si, Heng, and six other provinces, and inspector of Si Province; he inherited the dukedom of Ju and received the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 以晉公護子至為嗣。

translations.literal: Zhi, son of Duke of Jin Hu, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi, son of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 賓字乾瑞。

translations.literal: Bin, style Qianrui.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Qianrui.

sentences.zh: 尋坐直誅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was executed for a direct offense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was executed for a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，更以齊王憲子廣都公

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, again the Guangdu Gong, son of Prince of Qi Xian,
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande 6 (577), again the Guangdu Gong, son of Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian,

translations.literal: (Zhen)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhen)

sentences.zh: 〔貢〕襲爵。

translations.literal: [Gong] succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: [Gong] succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: (Zhen)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhen)

sentences.zh: 〔貢〕字乾禎。

translations.literal: [Gong], style Qianzhen.
translations.idiomatic: [Gong], styled Qianzhen.

sentences.zh: 宣帝初，被誅，國除。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuan's reign he was executed and the fief abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun's reign he was executed and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 虞國公仲，德皇帝從父兄也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhong of Yuguo, Zhong, was a paternal cousin of Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhong of Yuguo, Yuwen Zhong, was a paternal cousin of Emperor De.

sentences.zh: 卒於代。

translations.literal: He died in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dai.

sentences.zh: 保定初，追贈使持節、太傅、柱國大將軍、大司徒、大都督、燕平等十州諸軍事、燕州刺史；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was posthumously granted commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yan, Ping, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Yan Province;
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he was posthumously made commissioner bearing credentials, grand tutor, pillar-of-state general, grand minister of education, governor-general, commander-in-chief over Yan, Ping, and ten other provinces, and inspector of Yan Province;

sentences.zh: 封虞國公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: enfeoffed as Duke of Yuguo, with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed Duke of Yuguo, with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 子興嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 洛字永洛。

translations.literal: Luo, style Yongluo.
translations.idiomatic: Luo, styled Yongluo.

sentences.zh: 九歲，命為虞國公世子。

translations.literal: At nine years of age he was appointed heir to the Duke of Yuguo.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he was appointed heir to the Duke of Yuguo.

sentences.zh: 天和四年，詔襲興爵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhe, an edict had him inherit Xing's title.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe 4 (569) an edict made him inherit Xing's title.

sentences.zh: 建德初，拜使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande he was appointed commissioner bearing credentials, chariot-and-cavalry general, and grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jiande he was made commissioner bearing credentials, chariot-and-cavalry general, and grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 及靜帝崩，隋文帝以洛為介國公，為隋室賓云。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan died, Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian made Luo Duke of Jie, [saying he would be] a guest of the Sui house.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing Yuwen Chan died, Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian made Luo Duke of Jie, declaring that he would be a guest of the Sui house.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自古受命之君及守文之主，非獨異姓之輔也，亦有骨肉之助焉。

translations.literal: The historian writes: From antiquity, rulers who received the mandate and sovereigns who preserved the patrimony have relied not only on ministers of other surnames but also on assistance from flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From antiquity, founding rulers and heirs who kept the patrimony have relied not only on ministers outside the clan but also on help from royal kin.

sentences.zh: 其茂親有魯衛梁楚，其疏屬有凡蔣荊燕，咸能飛聲騰實，不泯於百代之後。

translations.literal: Among close kin were Lu, Wei, Liang, and Chu; among more distant kin were Fan, Jiang, Jing, and Yan—all could raise their fame and fulfill their worth and were not lost after a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Close royal houses such as Lu, Wei, Liang, and Chu, and more distant ones such as Fan, Jiang, Jing, and Yan, all won renown and proved their merit and were not forgotten after a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 至若豳孝公之勳烈，而加之以善政；

translations.literal: As for Duke Xiao of Bin's achievements of merit, to which was added good governance;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Duke Xiao of Bin's feats of arms, crowned by good government;

sentences.zh: 蔡文公之純孝，而飾之以儉約：峩峩焉，足以轥轢於前載矣。

translations.literal: and Duke Wen of Cai's pure filial piety, adorned with frugality: lofty indeed, enough to outshine the records of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: and Duke Wen of Cai's pure filial devotion, graced by thrift: towering figures, enough to eclipse the worthies of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 當隋氏之起，乘天威而服海內，將相王侯，莫不隳肝膽以效款，援符命以頌德。

translations.literal: When the Sui house rose, wielding Heaven's authority to subdue all within the seas, generals, ministers, kings, and marquises all dashed their hearts and livers in submission and invoked the mandate to praise its virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui house rose and, bearing Heaven's might, subdued the realm, generals, ministers, kings, and marquises all laid their lives open in submission and invoked the mandate to praise its virtue.

sentences.zh: 冑以葭莩之親，據一州而叶義舉，可謂忠而能勇。

translations.literal: Zhou, by reason of the closest kinship, held one province and joined the righteous rising—this may be called loyal and brave together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhou, by the closest kinship, held one province and joined the righteous rising—this may be called loyal and brave at once.

sentences.zh: 功業不遂，悲夫！

translations.literal: His enterprise went unfulfilled—alas!
translations.idiomatic: His enterprise went unfulfilled—alas!

sentences.zh: 亮實庸才，圖非常於巨逆。

translations.literal: Liang was truly a mediocrity who plotted extraordinary action amid great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was truly a mediocrity who plotted extraordinary action amid great treason.

sentences.zh: 古人稱不度德、不量力者，其斯之謂歟。

translations.literal: The ancients spoke of those who do not measure virtue and do not measure strength—is this not what they meant?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients spoke of men who do not measure their virtue or their strength—is this not exactly what they meant?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
